reference_title: Pavement Design for Roads, Streets, Walks, and Storage Areas

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Bituminous materials are asphalts or tars (UFC 3-250-03); tars are more temperature-susceptible but have better adhesion/penetration; asphalt surface courses are generally preferred; choice is normally economics-driven.
sections.body: The bituminous materials used in paving are asphaltic or tar products as listed in UFC 3-250-03. Although asphalts and tars resemble each other in general appearance, they do not have the same physical or chemical characteristics. Tars are affected to a greater extent by temperature changes and weather conditions; however, they tend to have better adhesive and penetrating properties than asphalts. Generally, asphalt surface courses are preferred to tar surface courses. The selection of the type of bituminous material (asphalt or tar) should normally be based on economy.
key_points: Asphalt vs. tar: tar is more temperature-sensitive but better adhesion/penetration; asphalt is the generally preferred surface course.
Selection is normally an economic decision.
sections.applicability: Choosing a bituminous binder family for a flexible surface course.

sections.title: Criteria for Bituminous Pavements
sections.summary: UFC 3-250-03 sets bitumen type/grade selection, aggregate requirements, quality requirements, and bituminous pavement types.
sections.body: The basic criteria for selection and design of bituminous pavements are contained in UFC 3-250-03 which includes the following criteria: selection of bitumen type; selection of bitumen grade; aggregate requirements; quality requirements; types of bituminous pavements.
key_points: UFC 3-250-03 is the governing document for bitumen type/grade/aggregate/quality/pavement-type selection.
sections.applicability: Cross-reference for detailed bituminous mix design criteria.

sections.title: Minimum Thickness
sections.summary: Where PCASE use is mandatory, minimum bituminous surface thickness varies with underlying base CBR per Table 7-2; refer to UFC 3-201-01 where a State procedure applies instead.
sections.body: Refer to UFC 3-201-01 for minimum thickness requirements where the State pavement design procedure is used. Where the use of PCASE is mandatory, the minimum thickness of bituminous materials varies with the strength of the underlying base course and is given in Table 7-2.
key_points: Minimum bituminous surface thickness is read from Table 7-2, keyed to base course CBR.
tables: Table 7-2: Minimum Thickness of Flexible Pavement Sections
sections.applicability: Checking minimum asphalt surface thickness for a given base CBR.
